Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:10:1.hebrew: הסול - קיסם שראשו חד, שקורין ברוק"א:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:10:1.english: The sol - A splinter whose tip is sharp, which they call broche.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:10:3.english: A gimlet - [That is,] taribele [in Old French, meaning a gimlet].

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:11:1.hebrew: אף כל של מתכת - ובפ"ק דקדושין מפרש פלוגתייהו: דרבי דריש כללי ופרטי, ור' יוסי דריש ריבויי ומיעוטי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:11:1.english: So too, anything of metal - And in the first chapter of Kiddushin, [the Gemara] explains their dispute: that Rabbi expounds [by means of] general and specific [principles], and Rabbi Yosei expounds [by means of] amplifications and limitations.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:13:1.english: In the earlobe - [That is, the] lobe [literally, fat tail, referring to the soft lobe of the ear].

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:13:2.english: How does it render [him] blemished - Behold, it heals back.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:13:3.hebrew: הא אין רוצעין - בניחותא. הא ודאי אין רוצעין אלא בגובה של אוזן, שהוא סחוס. ומכל מקום קשיא, דקתני הכא דמן הרציעה נעשה בעל מום, וקאמר רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה דרציעה ישנה במחט, דלא הוי כעדשה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:13:3.english: Behold, they pierce only - [This is stated] affirmatively: Indeed, they certainly pierce only in the upper part of the ear, which is cartilage. And nevertheless, the difficulty remains: for it teaches here that from the piercing he becomes blemished, and [yet] Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda said that piercing can be [performed] with a needle, which is not [as large as] a lentil.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:14:1.hebrew: כאן לשחוט כאן לפסול - יש מומין הרבה בבכור שפוסלים אותו ליקרב על גבי מזבח, ואין מכשירין אותו לישחט, כדתנן: אלו שאין שוחטין עליהן לא במקדש ולא במדינה כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:14:1.english: Here [with regard] to slaughtering; there [with regard] to disqualifying - There are many blemishes in a firstborn [animal] that disqualify it from being offered upon the altar, yet do not render it permitted to be slaughtered, as we learned in a Mishnah: “These are [the blemishes] on account of which one does not slaughter, neither in the Temple nor in the province...” etc.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:15:1.hebrew: הינדא - בלשון זה היו מכירין, ובלשון לע"ז — ויצ"א:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:15:1.english: Hinda - In this language they were familiar [with it], and in the vernacular [Old French]: vece [vetch].

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:16:1.hebrew: כרשינה - העומד בנקב בדוחק, ואע"פ שאינה נכנסת (עמו) ויוצאת בו, הוי מום? או דלמא לא הוי מום עד שיהא הנקב רחב שכרשינה תהא נכנסת ויוצאת בו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:16:1.english: A bitter vetch - [Does a bitter vetch] that stands in the hole with difficulty, even though it does not enter (with it) and exit through it, constitute a blemish? Or perhaps it does not constitute a blemish until the hole is wide [enough] that a bitter vetch can enter and exit through it?

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:16:2.hebrew: כיוצא בה שמעתי - מסיפא נפקא לן, דקאמר: מקדח וחיסומו שנינו, דהיינו נכנס ויוצא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:16:2.english: I heard a similar [halakha] to it - We derive [this] from the end [of the passage], where it says: "We learned [the measure of] a drill and its obstruction," which means entering and exiting.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:17:1.hebrew: השדרה והגולגולת - שלימין מטמאין באהל, ושאר עצמות אין מטמאין באהל. וכמה יחסרו ולא יטמאו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:17:1.english: The spine and the skull - [When] whole, they impart impurity in a tent, whereas other bones do not impart impurity in a tent. And how much may they be missing so that they will not impart impurity?

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:18:1.hebrew: ה"ג: ויתיב רב חסדא וקמיבעיא ליה, ואיתמר רב ספרא אמר שמעתא - א"ל רב תחליפא לרב חסדא, דהכי אתנייה שמואל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:18:1.english: This is the correct reading: "And Rav Ḥisda was sitting, and he raised a dilemma," and it was stated, "Rav Safra says [it was] an Amoraic tradition" - Rav Taḥlifa said to Rav Ḥisda that Shmuel taught him so.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:19:1.hebrew: וסימניך - שלא תטעה מי אמר שמעתא ומי מתניתא. תני רב יהודה בר שמואל — דאשכחן מקומות הרבה בש"ס דאיירי רב שמואל בר יהודה בל' מתניתא: תני רב שמואל בר יהודה במסכת ע"ז, רפואות דאין מעמידין (דף כח:):
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:19:1.english: And your mnemonic - So that you will not err [as to] who said a tradition and who [said] a baraita. "Rav Yehuda bar Shmuel teaches" — for we find many places in the Talmud where Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda speaks in the language of a baraita: "Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda teaches..." in tractate Avodah Zarah, [in the discussion of] remedies in [the chapter] Ein Ma'amidin (daf 28b).

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:1:1.english: It is not called an “ill blemish” - Except [when it is] exposed, which disfigures it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:1:2.english: If so - That “any blemish” is an amplification.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:1.hebrew: וא"ל - רב חסדא לרב תחליפא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:1.english: And he said to him - Rav Ḥisda [said this] to Rav Taḥlifa.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:2.hebrew: אם כן - דבית הלל כסלע אמר, עשית ב"ש וב"ה אחד:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:2.english: If so - That [Shmuel] said [that the measure of] Beit Hillel is like a sela — you have made Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel one [and the same].

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:3.hebrew: מאור - חלון. שלא נעשה בידי אדם — שנפל הכותל מאליו מעט בין בית לבית:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:3.english: A window - An aperture. "That was not fashioned by the hands of a person" — that the wall collapsed on its own a bit between one house and another.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:4.english: Its measure - To bring [ritual] impurity from this house to that house.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:5.hebrew: כמלא אגרוף גדול - דכיון דלא נעשה בידי אדם, בציר מהכי לא חשיב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:5.english: Like the fullness of a large fist - For since it was not made by human hands, [anything] less than this is not considered significant.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:6.hebrew: בן אבטיח - שם האיש, בעל בשר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:6.english: Ben Avatiaḥ - [This is] the name of the man, [who was] corpulent.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:20:7.english: And it is - [This refers] to that fist.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:21:1.english: Of the chamber - Which was kept in the chamber to drill whatever was needed for the maintenance of the Temple.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:21:2.hebrew: כפונדיון האיטלקי וכסלע נירונית - כלומר, לזה ולזה דומה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:21:2.english: Like the Italian pundeyon and like a Neronian sela - That is to say, it is similar to both this and that.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:21:3.english: And it is - [This refers] to that sela and to that pundeyon.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:2:1.english: Now, we do not redeem on account of them - [Namely,] consecrated animals that became disqualified.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:2:2.english: Will we slaughter on account of them? - [This refers to] a firstborn outside [the Temple].

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:3:1.hebrew: כשהוא אומר - פסוק אחר: "ואם בבהמה הטמאה ופדה בערכך":
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:3:1.english: When it states - [This is] another verse: “And if it be of an impure animal, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:5:1.hebrew: אם כן - דבעל מום עובר נמי נפדין, פסח ועור מאי אהני ליה? דמשמע מומין קבועין ולא עוברין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:5:1.english: If so - That [animals with] a temporary blemish are also redeemed, what purpose does "lame and blind" serve? For they imply permanent blemishes and not temporary [ones].

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:6:1.english: By the hand of Heaven - That [the animal] was born with it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:7:1.hebrew: שתחגור - שתעכב בה צפורן, אם בודקין כבדיקת סכין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:7:1.english: That [a fingernail] will catch - That a fingernail will be caught on it, if one checks [it] like the checking of a [slaughter] knife.

Rashi on Bekhorot 37b:9:1.english: Rather, of the first tanna and Rabbi Yosei - For a karshina is only slightly larger than a lentil.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:11:1.hebrew: לרבות כל דבר שנלקח ביד - בפרק קמא דקדושין (דף כא:) מפרש, משום דדריש ריבויי ומיעוטי: "ולקחת" — ריבה, "מרצע" — מיעט, "ונתת באזנו" — חזר וריבה. מאי רבי? רבי כל מילי. מאי מיעט? מיעט סם. ותימה: דמולקחת מרבינן כל דבר הנלקח ביד, ואם סם לא מקרי נלקח ביד — למה לי ריבה ומיעט וריבה? מלשון "ולקחת" לחוד לא מתרבי אלא דבר הנלקח ביד! וי"ל, דמלשון "ולקחת" לא דריש; אלא הכי קאמר: "לרבות כל דבר הנלקח ביד" — משום דדרשינן ריבויי ומיעוטי:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:11:1.english: "To include anything that is taken by hand" - In the first chapter of Kiddushin (21b), [the Gemara] explains [that Rabbi Yosei holds this] because he expounds [the verses via] amplifications and restrictions: "And you shall take" — [the verse] amplified; "an awl" — [it] restricted; "and you shall put [it] through his ear" — it amplified again. What did it amplify? It amplified [to include] everything. What did it restrict? It restricted [to exclude] a corrosive substance. And [this is] difficult: For from "and you shall take," we include anything that is taken by hand; and if a corrosive substance is not considered "taken by hand," why do I need [the derivation of] amplified, restricted, and amplified? From the phrasing of "and you shall take" alone, nothing is included except an item that is taken by hand! And one can say that he does not expound from the phrasing of "and you shall take" [itself]; rather, this is what [the Baraita] means: "To include anything that is taken by hand" — because we expound [the verses through] amplifications and restrictions.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:14:1.hebrew: כאן לשחוט כאן לפסול - מדפסיל כהן, משמע דהוי מום דאורייתא. ושמא האי דאין שוחטין — משום דאין ניכר יפה, וגזרינן אטו מומין שבסתר. אי נמי: האי דמפסיל כהן — משום דאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן. א"נ: מום עובר הוא, ובעינן שלא יפסל אפילו לפי שעה, משום דכתיב: "[ושב] אל משפחתו", דדרשי' בקדושין (שם): "למותר שבמשפחתו":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:14:1.english: "Here to slaughter, there to disqualify" - From [the fact] that it disqualifies a priest, it implies that it is a Torah-level blemish. And perhaps the reason that one does not slaughter [a firstborn animal on account of it] is because it is not clearly noticeable, and we decree [against it] on account of hidden blemishes. Alternatively, the fact that it disqualifies a priest is because it is not uniform among Aaron's offspring. Alternatively, it is a temporary blemish, and we require that he not be disqualified even temporarily, because it is written: "[And he shall return] to his family" (Leviticus 25:41), which we expound in Kiddushin (ibid.): "To the preeminent [status] in his family."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:17:1.hebrew: כדי שינטל מן החי וימות - ובכמלא מקדח וימות לב"ש? כדקאמר בפ"ק דעירובין (דף ז.): "וכן לטרפה", ומשמע דאתרוייהו קאי — אשדרה ואגולגולת! אלא ב"ה אתו למימר, דשיעורו כמלא מקדח הוי טפי מכדי שינטל מן החי וימות לדידהו. ורבינו תם נמי דמפרש דלא קאי "וכן לטרפה" אגולגולת — מדלא פריך בריש אלו טריפות (חולין דף מב:): "והאיכא כמה חסרון בגולגולת?!" כדפריך מחסרון בשדרה, משום דבנקיבת הקרום הוי טריפה בלא חסרון; והא דקרי בעירובין (דף ז.) שדרה וגולגולת "תרי חומרי דסתרי אהדדי", משום דהוו פליגי גבי טריפות דאדם, דאית ליה מזלא ואית ליה טפי חיות ולא מיטרף בנקיבת קרום בלא חסרון עמו — מ"מ לפירושו נמי צ"ל כן, כמו שפירשנו, דבשיעורא דב"ש ימות (לב"ש) כמו לב"ה בשיעורא דידהו. ומיהו, מה שמדקדק ר"ת מדלא פריך בריש אלו טריפות (חולין דף מב:) מחסרון דגולגולת — לאו פירכא הוא, דמצינן למימר דטריפות של חסרון לא הוי אלא משום דסופו של קרום לינקב, כמו ריאה דדמיא לדיותא ולכוחלא (שם מז:). ועוד קשה, לפי שמחלק בין דאדם לטרפות דבהמות — דבריש אלו טריפות (חולין מג.) מ להו דפריך להו מאיוב: "ישפוך לארץ מרירתי", ועדיין איוב קיים?! ומיהו הוה יכול ר"ת לפרש, דלא מטעם מזלא חשיב טריפה בבהמה טפי מאדם, אלא כגון דניקב קרום של מוח העליון ולא התחתון; ובבהמה קרום התחתון רך ואין מגין על המוח, אבל באדם התחתון קשה ומגין, משום הכי בעי חסרון עם נקיבת העליון; אבל בדבר ששוין בזה ובזה, אין לחלק ביניהם כלל:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:17:1.english: An amount that if removed from the living, he would die - And [if you ask]: Does he [not also] die with [a deficiency] the size of a drill hole according to Beit Shammai? For [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Eruvin (7a): "And so too for treifah," and it implies that this applies to both of them, to the spine and to the skull! Rather, Beit Hillel come to say that its measure of "the size of a drill hole" is greater than "an amount that if removed from the living, he would die" according to their view. And as for Rabbeinu Tam as well, who explains that "and so too for treifah" does not apply to the skull — because [the Gemara] at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Elu Tereifot (Chullin 42b) does not object: "And is there not [the case of] 'how much is a deficiency in the skull'?" as it objects from the deficiency in the spine, because with the perforation of the membrane [of the brain] it is a treifah without [any bone] deficiency; and that which [the Gemara] in Eruvin (7a) calls [the disputes over] the spine and the skull "two stringencies that contradict each other," [that is] because they disagreed regarding treifot of a human, who has a [spiritual] guardian [mazal] and has greater vitality, and does not become a treifah through perforation of the membrane without a deficiency [in the bone] along with it — nevertheless, according to his explanation as well, one must say so, as we explained: that with Beit Shammai's measure, [a person] dies according to Beit Shammai, just as according to Beit Hillel [he dies] with their measure. However, that which Rabbeinu Tam infers from the fact that [the Gemara] at the beginning of Elu Tereifot (Chullin 42b) does not object from the deficiency of the skull is no refutation; for we could say that the treifah status of [bone] deficiency is only because the membrane is ultimately destined to be perforated, like a lung that resembles ink or antimony (ibid. 47b). And furthermore, it is difficult [according to Rabbeinu Tam], since he differentiates between [treifot] of a human and treifot of animals — for at the beginning of Elu Tereifot (Chullin 43a), why was it that they challenged them from Job: "He pours out my gall upon the ground" (Job 16:13), and yet Job remained alive?! However, Rabbeinu Tam could have explained that it is not on account of mazal that [an injury] is considered a treifah in an animal more than in a human, but rather, for example, where the upper membrane of the brain was perforated and not the lower one; and in an animal the lower membrane is soft and does not protect the brain, but in a human the lower [membrane] is hard and protects [it] — on that account, he requires a deficiency [in the skull bone] along with the perforation of the upper [membrane]; but in a matter in which they are equal in both this and that, one should not distinguish between them at all.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:1:1.hebrew: נעקרו אין נפגמו ונגממו לא - הוי מצי לאתויי מההיא דלקמן, דקא חשיב בהדיא גבי "ואלו שאין שוחטין עליהן לא במקדש ולא במדינה": "חוטין הפנימיות שנפגמו ונגממו". אלא ניחא לאתויי מדיוקא דרישא, דמוכח דאע"ג דבחיצוניות הוי מום שבגלוי, בפנימיות לא הוי מום:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:1:1.english: "[If] they were extracted, yes; [if] they were damaged or chipped, no" - [The Gemara] could have cited [proof] from that [mishnah] later on, which explicitly lists among "And these are [the blemishes] for which they do not slaughter [the firstborn], neither in the Temple nor in the province": "internal gums that were damaged or chipped." Rather, it preferred to derive [it] from the inference of the first clause, which proves that even though in [the case of] the external [gums] it is an exposed blemish, in [the case of] the internal [gums] it is not a blemish.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:2:1.hebrew: השתא מיפרק לא פרקינן עילוי' כו' - וא"ת: להאי שנוייא קמא, דנפיק מום עובר מק"ו — "פסח ועור" מאי אהני ליה? וי"ל: דקסבר השתא, דאי לא כתיב "פסח ועור", קמרבינן מ"כל מום רע" מום עובר, והוה אמינא דאתא לאפוקי מק"ו, ולא ממעטינן נמי מ"מום רע" מומין שבסתר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 37b:2:1.english: "Now, we do not redeem on its account, etc." - And if you say: According to this first resolution, where a temporary blemish is derived [to be excluded] from an a fortiori argument, what did [the mention of] "lame and blind" accomplish? And one can say: For it [the Gemara] currently holds that had "lame and blind" not been written, we would include a temporary blemish from "any ill blemish," and I would say that it comes to preclude [the deduction of] the a fortiori argument; and we would not exclude hidden blemishes either from "an ill blemish."
